claims.title: The Saka 'Golden Man' of Issyk
claims.summary: A high-status Saka warrior is buried in the Issyk kurgan near Almaty in a costume of thousands of gold plaques, a celebrated emblem of the Iron Age nomad cultures that dominated the Kazakh steppe in the first millennium BCE.

sources.label: Ancient Sakas: All You Need to Know

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-400bce-the-saka-golden-man-of-issyk, claim TL:KAZ:event:400bce:the-saka-golden-man-of-issyk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turkic khaganates dominate the steppe
claims.summary: Turkic-speaking confederations, beginning with the Türk (Göktürk) Khaganate and later the Karakhanids, take control of the region; Zhetysu becomes a heartland of the Western Turkic realm, fixing the Turkic language and spreading Islam.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-552-turkic-khaganates-dominate-the-steppe, claim TL:KAZ:event:552:turkic-khaganates-dominate-the-steppe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Silk Road towns of the south flourish
claims.summary: Caravan cities such as Otrar, Taraz, Sauran, and Yasi prosper on the trade between China and the Mediterranean, becoming centres of commerce, craft, and Islamic learning along the southern Kazakh steppe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-999-silk-road-towns-of-the-south-flourish, claim TL:KAZ:event:999:silk-road-towns-of-the-south-flourish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol conquest of the Syr Darya and Khwarezm
claims.summary: Provoked by the killing of his envoys at Otrar, Genghis Khan storms the Silk Road towns and overruns Khwarezm; Otrar falls after a months-long siege, and the steppe is absorbed into the Mongol empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1219-mongol-conquest-of-the-syr-darya-and-khwarezm, claim TL:KAZ:event:1219:mongol-conquest-of-the-syr-darya-and-khwarezm, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Golden Horde rules the western steppe
claims.summary: The lands of present-day Kazakhstan pass to the line of Jochi, forming the western wing of the Mongol empire known as the Golden Horde, where Turks outnumber Mongols and Islam becomes the prevailing faith.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1242-the-golden-horde-rules-the-western-steppe, claim TL:KAZ:event:1242:the-golden-horde-rules-the-western-steppe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Timur builds the Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
claims.summary: At Yasi (Turkestan) Timur orders a monumental mausoleum over the tomb of the Sufi master Khoja Ahmed Yasawi; left unfinished at Timur's death in 1405, it became a masterpiece of Timurid architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1389-timur-builds-the-mausoleum-of-khoja-ahmed-yasawi, claim TL:KAZ:event:1389:timur-builds-the-mausoleum-of-khoja-ahmed-yasawi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the Kazakh Khanate
claims.summary: The Jochid sultans Janibek and Kerei break with Abu'l-Khayr Khan and lead their followers into Zhetysu, founding the Kazakh Khanate, the realm Kazakhs regard as the root of their nation and statehood.

sources.label: Establishment of the Kazakh Khanate
sources.publisher: Portal 'History of Kazakhstan' (e-history.kz), National Academic Library

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1465-foundation-of-the-kazakh-khanate, claim TL:KAZ:event:1465:foundation-of-the-kazakh-khanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The three jüz take shape
claims.summary: Kazakh society organises into three hordes, the Great, Middle, and Little jüz, each a confederation of tribes with its own pastures, united by language, Islam, and descent and headed by Genghisid khans.

sources.label: Establishment of the Kazakh Khanate
sources.publisher: Portal 'History of Kazakhstan' (e-history.kz), National Academic Library

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1500-the-three-juz-take-shape, claim TL:KAZ:event:1500:the-three-juz-take-shape, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 'Great Disaster' of the Dzungar wars
claims.summary: Devastating invasions by the Buddhist Dzungar confederation drive Kazakhs from their pastures with great loss of life, an episode remembered as the Aktaban Shubyryndy that gravely weakens the khanate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1723-the-great-disaster-of-the-dzungar-wars, claim TL:KAZ:event:1723:the-great-disaster-of-the-dzungar-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Little Horde accepts Russian protection
claims.summary: Abu'l-Khayr Khan of the Little Horde swears allegiance to the Russian Empire for protection against the Dzungars; the Middle Horde follows in 1740 and part of the Great Horde in 1742, opening the steppe to Russian power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1731-the-little-horde-accepts-russian-protection, claim TL:KAZ:event:1731:the-little-horde-accepts-russian-protection, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ablai Khan elected ruler of the Kazakhs
claims.summary: Ablai (Abylai) is elected khan of the Kazakhs and balances between the Russian and Qing empires to preserve a degree of independence; he endures as a national symbol of Kazakh sovereignty.

sources.label: Abylai the King: A Warrior, Diplomat and Patriot
sources.publisher: Portal 'History of Kazakhstan' (e-history.kz), National Academic Library

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1771-ablai-khan-elected-ruler-of-the-kazakhs, claim TL:KAZ:event:1771:ablai-khan-elected-ruler-of-the-kazakhs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russia abolishes the Kazakh khanates
claims.summary: To end Kazakh autonomy, Russia abolishes the khanate of the Middle Horde in 1822, the Little Horde in 1824, and the Great Horde in 1848, dismantling the political structure of the Kazakh Khanate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1822-russia-abolishes-the-kazakh-khanates, claim TL:KAZ:event:1822:russia-abolishes-the-kazakh-khanates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kenesary Kasymov's revolt
claims.summary: Kenesary Kasymov, a grandson of Ablai Khan, leads the largest Kazakh uprising against Russian rule, fighting to restore the independent khanate until he is killed in 1847.

sources.label: Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1837-kenesary-kasymov-s-revolt, claim TL:KAZ:event:1837:kenesary-kasymov-s-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kazakh famine (Asharshylyk)
claims.summary: Forced collectivisation and the settling of nomads under Filipp Goloshchekin produce a man-made famine that kills an estimated 1.5 million people, around a third of all Kazakhs, the deadliest catastrophe in Kazakh history; the toll is an estimate.

sources.label: The Kazakh Famine of the 1930s
sources.publisher: Library of Congress (John W. Kluge Center)

sources.label: The Hungry Steppe: Famine, Violence, and the Making of Soviet Kazakhstan
sources.publisher: Library of Congress (John W. Kluge Center)

claims.title: Kazakh S.S.R. becomes a union republic
claims.summary: Kazakhstan, an autonomous republic since 1920 and renamed the Kazak A.S.S.R. in 1925, is raised to a full constituent republic of the Soviet Union under the 1936 constitution.

sources.label: Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1936-kazakh-s-s-r-becomes-a-union-republic, claim TL:KAZ:event:1936:kazakh-s-s-r-becomes-a-union-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Semipalatinsk nuclear test site
claims.summary: The Soviet Union conducts some 456 nuclear tests at the Semipalatinsk site in northeastern Kazakhstan between 1949 and 1989, exposing local populations to radioactive fallout with severe long-term health effects.

sources.label: Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1949-semipalatinsk-nuclear-test-site, claim TL:KAZ:event:1949:semipalatinsk-nuclear-test-site, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khrushchev's Virgin Lands campaign
claims.summary: Nikita Khrushchev's drive to plough up the northern Kazakh steppe for grain brings hundreds of thousands of mostly Slavic settlers, transforming the republic's demography so that Kazakhs become a minority in Kazakhstan.

sources.label: Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1954-khrushchev-s-virgin-lands-campaign, claim TL:KAZ:event:1954:khrushchev-s-virgin-lands-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kazakhstan declares independence
claims.summary: Kazakhstan proclaims itself a sovereign, independent state, the last of the Soviet republics to declare independence, with Nursultan Nazarbayev as president; the USSR formally dissolves days later.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1991-kazakhstan-declares-independence, claim TL:KAZ:event:1991:kazakhstan-declares-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital moved to Astana
claims.summary: Nazarbayev relocates the capital from Almaty to Akmola on the northern steppe; renamed Astana ('capital') in 1998, it is rebuilt as a planned showcase city of modern architecture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-1997-capital-moved-to-astana, claim TL:KAZ:event:1997:capital-moved-to-astana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nazarbayev resigns; Tokayev succeeds
claims.summary: After nearly three decades in power, Nazarbayev steps down as president, handing office to Kassym-Jomart Tokayev while retaining major influence; the capital is briefly renamed Nur-Sultan in his honour.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-2019-nazarbayev-resigns-tokayev-succeeds, claim TL:KAZ:event:2019:nazarbayev-resigns-tokayev-succeeds, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: 'Bloody January' unrest
claims.summary: Protests over fuel prices spread nationwide and turn violent; Tokayev declares a state of emergency, summons CSTO troops, and authorises lethal force, with about 227 deaths reported, then sidelines Nazarbayev's allies to consolidate power.

sources.label: A regime transition in action: Bloody January in Kazakhstan

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kazakhstan: From the Saka horsemen of the Great Steppe to the world's largest landlocked nation.", terralore.co/country/KAZ/chronicle#ev-2022-bloody-january-unrest, claim TL:KAZ:event:2022:bloody-january-unrest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
